text:
Allison Grant: pulling folks into a quick thread on alert thresholds for *Dedicated staged rollouts* (paused rollouts + evaluator lag). we’ve got draft dashboards up, but need to lock paging vs ticket-only and thresholds before dogfood expands.

Allison Grant: dashboards draft (WIP): https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/dedicated-rollouts-gates/overview
Allison Grant: alert rules PR (observability-pack): https://github.com/redwoodinference/observability-pack/pull/913
Allison Grant: goals:
- detect rollouts stuck/paused in a way that hurts customers
- detect gate evaluator lag / metrics staleness before we make a bad decision
- avoid paging on noise (we already page on pool health separately)

Sean Gallagher: :+1: been hearing from oncall that “paused” is ambiguous right now. we need to page only when it’s impacting a real rollout, not every paused plan sitting around.

Rafael Mendes: agreed. also what’s the expected “pause” duration? if a human approval is required, a pause could be normal. if it’s auto-hold due to gate fail/missing metrics, that’s more urgent.

Allison Grant: yep. proposal is to alert on *state + reason*. current states we get from console backend are:
- IN_PROGRESS
- HOLD (with hold_reason)
- PAUSED (manual)
- ABORTED
- COMPLETED
and hold reasons: GATE_FAILED, METRICS_MISSING, EVALUATOR_DEGRADED, CAPACITY_GUARDRAIL

Logan Wright: from telemetry side, “METRICS_MISSING” will happen during deploys and occasionally during ingestion blips. if we page on that at low duration we’ll wake everyone up for nothing.

Thomas Baird: +1. evaluator loop also has some jitter during compactions. we should differentiate lag vs total stop.

Allison Grant: ok let’s break it down:
(1) evaluator lag / health
(2) rollout “stuck” in HOLD/PAUSED too long
(3) high rate of auto-holds / false positives

Sean Gallagher: evaluator lag should probably be P1 only if it blocks advancement *and* we have active rollouts. otherwise P2/ticket.

Allison Grant: what are we measuring for evaluator lag in PR 913 right now:
- `rollout_gate_evaluator_last_success_ts` (per env)
- `rollout_gate_evaluator_tick_duration_seconds_p95`
- `rollout_gate_evaluator_eval_delay_seconds` (now - window_end)
- `rollout_gate_evaluator_query_errors_total`

Logan Wright: the one i trust most is eval_delay_seconds (if it’s >window + some buffer, we’re making decisions on stale data).

Thomas Baird: careful: delay can be expected when window_end is “now-2m” (depending on window alignment). but once it’s > 2x eval interval, it’s bad.

Allison Grant: current config for dogfood:
- evaluation interval: 60s
- typical windows: 5m w/ “require 4/5 mins present”
- metrics pipeline: ~30-90s latency

Rafael Mendes: if metrics pipeline is 90s worst case, evaluator will be “late” but not broken. so alert should be like >5m not >90s.

Sean Gallagher: can we set two levels?
- warn: eval_delay > 3m for 10m (slack + ticket)
- page: eval_delay > 10m for 5m AND active_rollouts>0

Allison Grant: that maps well. i can express active rollouts via `dedicated_rollout_active_count` (from console aggregation) which is in the PR.

Chloe Martin: fyi `dedicated_rollout_active_count` is only for staged rollouts feature-flagged tenants right now. but that’s fine for paging gating; if it’s 0, no page.

Mina Haddad: routing side: if evaluator is degraded we force HOLD (per fail-safe). that’s the correct behavior but will stop progression. we should page if we’re blocking a rollout that someone is trying to push.

Allison Grant: cool.

Allison Grant: (2) “paused rollout too long”:
- manual PAUSED should not page by default
- HOLD with reasons above should page if sustained + active

Rafael Mendes: +1. also “CAPACITY_GUARDRAIL” hold might mean we’re out of headroom and the rollout can’t proceed. that might be urgent because it can indicate sizing issue.

Sean Gallagher: i’d page for CAPACITY_GUARDRAIL if it’s a production tenant (not staging) and it’s blocking >15m.

Allison Grant: we have env + pool labels, and tenant tier label (internal/beta/enterprise) in the metrics. do we want to route enterprise to pager, beta to slack?

Sean Gallagher: yes. enterprise: page. internal/beta: slack channel + ticket.

PagerDuty: (system) Reminder: SRE Primary rotation changes in 2 days. Update runbooks before new feature pages.

Allison Grant: :grimacing: ok.

Allison Grant: proposed alert matrix (initial):
A) EvaluatorDegradedPage
- condition: `rollout_gate_evaluator_eval_delay_seconds > 600` for 5m
- AND `dedicated_rollout_active_count > 0`
- AND env=prod
- severity: page (P1)

B) EvaluatorLagWarn
- condition: `rollout_gate_evaluator_eval_delay_seconds > 180` for 10m
- env in (prod, staging)
- severity: slack + ticket

C) RolloutHoldGateFailed
- condition: `dedicated_rollout_hold_count{hold_reason="GATE_FAILED"} > 0` for 10m
- AND active_count > 0
- env=prod
- severity: page for enterprise tenants; slack/ticket otherwise

D) RolloutHoldMetricsMissing
- condition: hold_reason=METRICS_MISSING for 20m
- AND active_count > 0
- env=prod
- severity: ticket + slack; page only if >60m

E) RolloutHoldCapacityGuardrail
- condition: hold_reason=CAPACITY_GUARDRAIL for 15m
- env=prod
- severity: page enterprise; slack/ticket otherwise

F) RolloutStuckInProgress
- condition: stage_state=IN_PROGRESS but no stage_transition events for 30m
- severity: ticket (noise risk)

Thoughts?

Thomas Baird: evaluator delay >600s seems reasonable. but add a “no data” guard. sometimes prometheus restarts and it’ll show absent.

Allison Grant: yep PR 913 uses `absent()` guard. if series is absent entirely, we fire a different alert “MetricsPipelineDown” which already exists.

Logan Wright: for METRICS_MISSING: i’d keep it non-paging unless it’s blocking enterprise. 60m page is ok, but we should also surface % missing metrics per pool so oncall can tell if it’s just one label explosion.

Allison Grant: dashboard has panel “metrics freshness p50/p95 by env” + “missing samples ratio”. linking screenshot in PR comments.

Sean Gallagher: for GATE_FAILED holds: paging SRE might be wrong if it’s actually an app regression (model change) not infra. maybe page the rollout operator (eng-platform) first?

Rafael Mendes: +1. in practice if gate fails, first responder should be whoever initiated rollout. SRE should only be paged if it’s causing customer impact or we suspect telemetry/evaluator issue.

Mina Haddad: agree. but if it’s enterprise and rollouts are run by ops, that might still be SRE. maybe route to #eng-platform-oncall for gate fails, SRE for evaluator degraded/capacity guardrail.

Allison Grant: that’s fair. i can route alerts by label `hold_reason`. e.g.
- GATE_FAILED => eng-platform oncall (slack + pager depending tenant tier)
- EVALUATOR_DEGRADED / eval_delay => SRE
- CAPACITY_GUARDRAIL => SRE + infra (since it’s headroom policy)

Sean Gallagher: yes please. i don’t want paged for “gate failed because p95 latency actually got worse” unless the customer is currently down.

Chloe Martin: we can add `initiator` and `last_approver` to the alert annotations (from rollout plan audit events). might help with “who to ping”. not sure if it’s in metrics yet.

Allison Grant: not in metrics currently. could add as alert annotation via link to rollout detail view in console (includes initiator + audit trail). e.g. `https://console.redwoodinference.com/dedicated/pools/<pool_id>/rollouts/<rollout_id>`

Rafael Mendes: that’s enough.

Sean Gallagher: what about “paused rollouts” specifically? the description mentions paused rollouts. do we want any alert for manual pause?

Allison Grant: i’d do a *non-paging* reminder:
- if state=PAUSED and active_count>0 for >24h => ticket
reason: someone paused and forgot.

Logan Wright: +1. that’s normal behavior.

Thomas Baird: for evaluator lag warn (180s for 10m) - might still be noisy during deploy windows. can we add “exclude deploy train” label? :)

Allison Grant: lol. not easily. but we can add `for: 20m` to reduce noise. would that still be useful?

Sean Gallagher: warn at 180s for 20m is fine. paging at 600s for 5m stays.

Allison Grant: ok updating:
B) EvaluatorLagWarn: >180s for 20m

Rafael Mendes: can we add an alert for “high false-positive holds”? i.e. holds that clear themselves quickly (like hold for missing metrics for <2m) but happen repeatedly.

Allison Grant: i added a panel for “hold events rate by reason”. we could alert on spike:
- `rate(dedicated_rollout_hold_events_total{hold_reason="METRICS_MISSING"}[15m]) > N`
Need N though.

Logan Wright: start with dashboard-only. we don’t have baseline. once dogfood runs for a week we’ll know.

Sean Gallagher: agree, don’t page on brand new rate alert.

Allison Grant: action items:
- [AG] update PR 913 thresholds + routing notes
- [SG/RM] confirm paging destinations (SRE vs eng-platform) w/ Connor (release eng)
- [LW/TB] sanity-check that labels used are low-cardinality (pool_id is scary)

Thomas Baird: pool_id in alert labels is ok if we keep it in annotations only and group by env/tenant_tier. don’t want a million alert instances.

Allison Grant: yep. rules are aggregated; pool_id only as “top offenders” link in dashboard.

Sean Gallagher: can you also add runbook links in annotations? oncall needs a one-click.

Allison Grant: will do. runbook draft link for now: https://confluence.redwoodinference.internal/display/SRE/Runbook+-+Dedicated+Rollout+Holds

Rafael Mendes: make sure it includes “check metrics freshness first” step. last incident we chased a ghost because metrics were delayed.

Allison Grant: adding.

Mina Haddad: small note: routing will prevent stage advancement when evaluator degraded (by design). so eval_delay page should tell operator: “expected behavior is HOLD; do not force-advance.”

Allison Grant: good call. adding annotation text.

Chloe Martin: fyi console shows “Evaluator behind by X min” in stage detail. if we keep alert threshold aligned w/ that UI, fewer confused pings.

Allison Grant: ok i’ll align UI copy with >3m warn and >10m page wording.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: once PR is updated i’ll approve from SRE side.

Allison Grant: pushed updates to PR 913 w/ revised thresholds and routing notes. https://github.com/redwoodinference/observability-pack/pull/913#issuecomment-XXXXX

Logan Wright: reviewed labels in PR. looks ok. please don’t add `rollout_id` label anywhere.

Allison Grant: confirmed, no rollout_id labels.

Rafael Mendes: re paging destinations: for enterprise CAPACITY_GUARDRAIL holds, page SRE; for GATE_FAILED, page eng-platform; for METRICS_MISSING warn -> slack + ticket, no page. works for me.

Sean Gallagher: same. final nit: for EVALUATOR_DEGRADED, page SRE but auto-add @eng-platform in slack notification.

Allison Grant: done.

Allison Grant: closing the loop: thresholds locked for dogfood:
- eval_delay warn: >3m for 20m
- eval_delay page: >10m for 5m + active_rollouts>0
- hold(GATE_FAILED): notify eng-platform oncall if >10m + active>0 (page only enterprise)
- hold(METRICS_MISSING): ticket/slack at 20m; page enterprise only if >60m
- hold(CAPACITY_GUARDRAIL): page enterprise at 15m

Allison Grant: please shout if oncall sees noise after we flip the next pool. we’ll tune after 48h.

Sean Gallagher: :+1: thanks. will add a note to oncall handoff.
